headline: Recovery is improving; keep today deliberately short
summary: Last night's completed Garmin record shows strong autonomic recovery: sleeping heart rate fell below both recent baselines, Body Battery reached 91, and Training Readiness rose to 77. Because the marathon was only four days ago and Monday added another 7 km, use those good signals to permit a short recovery test—not to resume normal training.

recovery.label: Sleep
recovery.context: Good quality, but duration was only fair; deep sleep was 1h 35m and REM 1h 22m.

recovery.label: Sleeping HR
recovery.context: About 2.9 bpm below both the prior 7-night average (64.9) and prior 14-night average (64.7).

recovery.label: Resting HR
recovery.context: 1 bpm below the seven-day average of 59 and down from 62 yesterday.

recovery.label: HRV
recovery.context: Garmin rates the HRV contribution very good; the snapshot does not expose a separate nightly HRV value.

recovery.label: Body Battery
recovery.context: Charged 69 points overnight, a substantial rebound from 32 after the marathon.

recovery.label: Training Readiness
recovery.context: Garmin reports well recovered; remaining recovery time is only 20 minutes.

recovery.label: Stress
recovery.context: Low and reassuring, but today's value covers only the morning and is not comparable with a full day.

yesterday.title: Rest day
yesterday.summary: No activity was recorded on 2 September. Over the seven days ending today, running totals 55.0 km across three runs with about 727 load points; including Saturday's ride, recorded activity load is about 813. The marathon supplied 513 load points and remains the dominant stress.

recommendation.title: 20–25 minute flat recovery test
details: Run only if walking and stairs are normal, energy feels ordinary, and there is no focal medial-ankle or arch pain.
Keep it conversational at RPE 2–3 on flat, predictable ground. Let pace float; roughly 6:30–7:15/km is a ceiling guide, not a target.
Do not add strides, hills, tempo work, extra distance, or loaded calf/foot strength today.
Finish feeling that another 10–15 minutes would have been easy.
recommendation.alternative: Take complete rest or walk gently for 20–30 minutes if your legs still feel beaten up, sleepiness is prominent, or any symptom gate fails.
recommendation.reduce_or_stop: Keep posterior-tibial discomfort at 0–2/10 and stable. Stop immediately if it rises, becomes sharp or localised, changes your stride, or produces worsening pain later today or tomorrow morning. Swelling, illness, altered gait, or medical advice overrides Garmin scores.

signals.label: Sleeping-HR recovery
signals.interpretation: A roughly 3 bpm fall below the previous seven-night average supports genuine overnight recovery rather than relying on readiness alone.

signals.label: Readiness and recharge
signals.interpretation: Both have rebounded strongly, supporting a small return-to-running test if symptoms are normal.

signals.label: Residual race stress
signals.interpretation: The marathon was only four days ago and dominates the week's load, so connective-tissue and muscular recovery still justify a strict duration cap.

caveats: Today's stress value is incomplete because the snapshot was generated during the Sydney morning.
The snapshot provides Garmin's weekly HRV average and factor rating but not a separate nightly HRV measurement.
The 31 August wrist-heart-rate trace remains internally inconsistent (145 bpm average, 190 bpm maximum), so it is not used to prescribe today's intensity.
